question: Very recently, the Greek Government passed a provision1 giving the go-ahead for 37 500 ‘free’ afternoon surgeries to be funded by the Recovery and Resilience Fund. The provision in question states, among other things, that ‘the implementing body may, for the purposes of the project and following a call for expressions of interest, contract with private facilities that perform surgeries (day hospitals).

Payment takes the form of a subsidy granted to the relevant implementing body and the sum is paid to the participating private facilities that perform the surgeries.’ The same provision refers to the inclusion of the initiative in question, titled ‘Organisational reforms in the healthcare system’ (measure ID: 16756), under the Greece 2.0 Recovery and Resilience Fund2.

In the relevant Council document3, measure 16756 includes two projects (sequential numbers 163 and 164) with the following names/descriptions: ‘Health system – finalise the Greek DRG Institute KETEKNY and the new Agency for Quality Assurance in Healthcare ODIPY (excl. Training)’ and ‘Health system – KETEKNY ODIPY complete training’.

Given that it is not clear from the name/description of the above measure4 that there is precise alignment with the legislative initiative in question, can the Commission answer the following: Has the Fund approved funding for surgeries in private healthcare facilities under the abovementioned measure?

For the full text, see Article 2 https://drive.google.com/file/d/1HIIyk0PH8oZ6QfNIYpQKBZREZgXnVeK/view?pli=1. ‘In the context of the project ... (Measure: ‘Organisational Reforms in the Health System (measure ID: 16756)’) under the Greece 2.0 Recovery and Resilience Fund ...

payment shall be made for pending surgery and other interventions to be undergone by eligible patients (‘beneficiaries’) who have been registered on the Single List of Surgeries for a period longer than four (4) months.’ https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15831-2023-ADD-1-REV-1/en/pdf. See description of reform 16756 on p. 113 of the annex in the document cited in footnote 3.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.2.2025) On 21 January 2024, the Council adopted the Council Implementation Decision amending the Implementing Decision of 13 July 2021 on the approval of the assessment of the recovery and resilience plan for Greece. A subproject related to afternoon surgeries was introduced under measure 16756 (Organisational Reforms in the Health System) under component 3.

3 (Improve resilience, accessibility and sustainability of healthcare). The main objective of the subproject is the reduction of the waiting list for elective surgeries. More specifically, this allocates EUR 51 million of the Recovery and Resilience Facility grants to fund the operational cost of 37,500 afternoon surgeries. Priority would be given to patients that have been waiting the longest.

Afternoon surgeries will be performed in public hospitals. The subproject also provides that for cases where it will not be possible to carry out the surgeries in the hospital, the surgery may be carried out in another public hospital in proximity, or in a collaborating private hospital.

If the possibility for the surgery to take place in a private hospital is activated, it will be the citizen who will choose the private provider from a list which will include all collaborating hospitals. The Greek National Health Service Organisation (ΕΟPYY) has the main responsibility for the implementation of afternoon surgeries in private hospitals.

The Ministry of Health is the supervising authority for the implementation of the entire project. The target associated with this subproject (T164a) is expected to be completed by the fourth quarter of 2025 and submitted as part of Greece’s ninth payment request.
